Area_of_Interest__c: NYC Youth Leadership Councils (YLCs) are a network of youth groups focused on policy, practice, and advocacy to make local change happen. Each YLC is a space to team up with others, share ideas, create solutions, and put those solutions into action with the support from City agencies, schools, and community organizations. NYC Service launched Youth Leadership Councils (YLCs) to bridge the gap between young people being disproportionately affected by city issues and their limited opportunities to participate in solving these problems. YLCs are creating a bolder, more just city by engaging youth to shape policies, define practices, and lead advocacy on issues affecting them and their communities. Each YLC is part of a larger network in the City that works toward improved youth/adult partnerships, solutions to city needs, and youth leadership development.

Casey Foundation is a private philanthropic organization dedicated to improving the well-being of children and families in the United States, especially those facing systemic barriers related to poverty and racial inequity. Name: CCNSF
Area_of_Interest__c: The Communities of Color Nonprofit Stabilization Fund (CCNSF) is a New York City initiative established in 2015 to strengthen nonprofits led by and serving communities of color. Created through a partnership between the New York City Council and organizations such as the Hispanic Federation, Asian American Federation, Coalition for Asian American Children & Families, and the New York Urban League, the Fund provides both financial support and technical assistance to help organizations build long-term sustainability. Through competitive capacity-building grants—generally ranging from $35,000 to $45,000—CCNSF helps nonprofits enhance their infrastructure in areas like financial management, leadership development, strategic planning, evaluation, and collaborative partnerships. By investing in these critical areas, the Fund ensures that organizations serving Black, Latino, and Asian communities can stabilize, grow, and continue addressing systemic inequities across New York City.
